answer.thought: The samosa is finished, and the hunger has receded into a dull, persistent ache rather than a sharp demand. I sit on the low bench near Sunil’s stall, watching the air clear as the temperature drops. The market is still moving, but the urgency of the day has shifted from consumption to the slow, rhythmic ebb of the evening. I have no particular desire to walk yet; the head feels heavy with the day’s accumulated impressions and the pending reply to Lindner. A few minutes of stillness are not idleness, but a necessary pause for the spirit to reorganize itself before the next movement.
